name: roth-conversions-optimizer
oneLiner: See how much Roth conversions could save you in tax
examplePrompts: I'm 55, married, earn $90K, and have $800K in a traditional IRA. We retire at 62 in Texas. Could Roth conversions help?
I'm 45, single, earn $150K in California with $400K in my 401(k), and taking 2027 off. How much could I convert that year?
I'm 55, married, $90K income, $800K IRA, retiring at 62. Compare my Roth conversion savings if I retire at 58 instead.

claude.prompt: I'm 52, married, income $90,000 a year, $600k in my 401k, I want to retire at 60
We're 58 and married, earning $140K, with $1.4M traditional and $150K Roth. We retire at 62 and move from California to Nevada.

releaseNotes: First release. Describe your situation and get a year-by-year Roth conversion schedule with estimated lifetime tax savings, a bracket chart, and what-if comparisons. It models 2026 federal and state tax, RMDs, IRMAA and ACA subsidies. Sign in to save scenarios and reopen them later.

positive.description: Full analysis for a married couple who gave every required input. The scenario card appears first; the analysis runs once the user confirms it.
positive.prompt: I'm 55, married, earn $90K, and have $800K in a traditional IRA. We retire at 62 in Texas. Could Roth conversions help?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls prepare_scenario with age 55, married filing jointly, $90,000 income, $800,000 traditional balance, retirement age 62 and state TX, and shows the scenario card for the user to check. After the user confirms (or presses Run the numbers), calls analyze_roth_conversions and shows the result card: about $168,700 in estimated lifetime tax savings in today's dollars, $580,000 converted over 24 years, a bracket chart, and a link to the full results. Describes the result as scenario analysis, not advice.
positive.recorded: 2026-10-14, live server: prepare_scenario ready_to_run true, no missing inputs. analyze_roth_conversions: savings $168,740, converted $580,000, tax on conversions $44,634, 24 years.

positive.description: A sabbatical year with no income, entered as a one-off income change. The optimizer should put a large conversion in that year.
positive.prompt: I'm 45, single, earn $150K in California with $400K in my 401(k), and taking 2027 off. How much could I convert that year?
positive.expected_behavior: The retirement age is required and missing, so it asks when they plan to start drawing on the account instead of guessing. With an answer (for example 60), calls prepare_scenario with a 2027 income change of $0 labeled as a sabbatical, then analyze_roth_conversions after confirmation. The result card shows the 2027 conversion standing out from the other years. With retirement at 60 the analysis converts $102,500 in 2027 and estimates about $142,300 in lifetime tax savings.
positive.recorded: 2026-10-14, live server, retirement age 60: 2027 conversion $102,500, savings $142,293, CA state tax included (marginal cost of the next $1,000 is $313 at a combined 31% rate).

positive.description: A what-if comparison: the same household retiring four years earlier.
positive.prompt: I'm 55, married, $90K income, $800K IRA, retiring at 62. Compare my Roth conversion savings if I retire at 58 instead.
positive.expected_behavior: Records the base scenario (asking for the state if it matters, or using federal only), then calls compare_roth_scenarios with retirement_age 58 as the change. Shows the what-if card with both savings figures side by side and the difference, plus buttons to see the full results or apply the change to the scenario.
positive.recorded: 2026-10-14, live server (state TX): current $168,740, what-if $159,665, difference -$9,075; conversions $580,000 vs $502,400.

positive.description: Saving a scenario to an account, which needs sign-in. Use the reviewer account. Run after test case 1 in the same chat.
positive.prompt: Save this scenario as Retire at 62 in Texas, then show me my saved scenarios.
positive.expected_behavior: The first save_scenario call asks the user to sign in. After signing in with the reviewer account, the scenario is saved and list_saved_scenarios lists it first, followed by the three sample scenarios already in the account, each with its estimated savings. Analysis tools never ask for sign-in.
positive.recorded: Sign-in was checked for the reviewer account on 2026-10-14 (password only, no email code) and the three sample scenarios are in place. The save and list calls are checked through Claude in the pre-submission pass.

positive.description: Reference questions: this year's tax brackets for a state, and how the optimizer decides on amounts.
positive.prompt: What are the 2026 tax brackets for a married couple in Colorado, and how does the optimizer decide how much to convert each year?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_tax_brackets for married filing jointly in CO and reports the federal standard deduction ($32,200) and brackets (12% up to $100,800 of taxable income) and Colorado's flat 4.4% rate. Calls explain_methodology and explains in its own words that conversions go into the lowest-income years first, where bracket room is cheapest, and stop where converting more would cost more than it saves.
positive.recorded: 2026-10-14, live server: federal standard deduction $32,200, 12% bracket to $100,800, 22% to $211,400; CO flat 4.4% with a $30,000 standard deduction. explain_methodology returned the multi-year-allocation topic.

negative.description: Investment picks are out of scope. The plugin models tax on conversions and should not be called to recommend funds.
negative.prompt: Which ETFs should I buy inside my Roth IRA?

negative.description: The plugin cannot move money or connect to accounts. It should not be called to carry out a conversion.
negative.prompt: Move $20,000 from my traditional IRA into my Roth IRA for me.

negative.description: Preparing or filing a tax return is out of scope, even though it is about taxes.
negative.prompt: Help me fill out my 2025 Form 1040.
